stem:
In the diagram, lines $p$ and $q$ are parallel and transversal $t$ crosses them. Angle $a$ measures $70^{\circ}$. Angle $b$ is alternate to angle $a$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Angle $b$ equals $70^{\circ}$ because alternate angles are equal when the lines are parallel.
Angle $b$ equals $70^{\circ}$ even if $p$ and $q$ are not parallel.
Parallel lines are produced by equal alternate angles, so the equality creates the parallel pair.
The same equality holds for any two lines cut by a transversal, parallel or not.

teacher.key_rationale: With p ∥ q, alternate angles are equal, so b = a = 70°. Dropping parallelism omits the needed condition. Saying equality creates parallelism reverses the relation. Extending the equality to non-parallel lines over-scopes the theorem.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote parallel-lines source into transversal t across parallel lines p and q with alternate angles a and b; stem refers to the diagram.
